spec.question: E206 measured which number the delta-token gate cannot see. The level-quote gate has the opposite blind spot: it classes numeric leaves BY NAME, so a count that happens to be spelled `gap_sessions` becomes a fabricated bp quote. This leg asks every published face which of its measurement-named cells could not be a quote at all.
spec.scan: results/**/*.json below the size cap, ['/_quarantine/'] excluded

buckets.boolean: a flag published under a measurement name
buckets.count_word: an integer whose own name says 'a number of things'
buckets.small_integer: an exact integer with no count word and |v| <= 100 -- most likely a count, a coarse quote possible, so it is a candidate and not a verdict
buckets.integral_quote_sized: an exact integer above the ceiling: 5,776 bp is a real reading, so this is NOT counted against the page
buckets.quote_shaped: non-integral: the shape a derived bp quote actually has

spec.read_as: level_class() applied to the same name, i.e. what the existing name-based auditor would file the cell as
spec.changes_nothing: nothing is rewritten and no number is re-derived; this is an inventory of a name-channel hazard

honest: integrality is a SIGNATURE of a count, not proof: a bp value of exactly 0.0 lands in small_integer, and 0.0 is a real quote. The ceiling is a line this leg draws, so the sensitivity table publishes what the headline would be if the line moved to [10, 100, 1000]
the count-word list is a word test, so a count spelled without a count word (`gap` = 71) is only ever reported as small_integer -- the ambiguity is the finding, not a defect in the reader
the sweep is bounded by a size cap and reports how many faces it skipped, so the totals are a floor on the surface, never a claim of completeness
this leg cannot tell whether any individual number is wrong; it answers only 'could a reader quote this as bp'
law_ref: O-20260924-1626 R3 (a name-based audit may not invent a quote) + E180/E206 self-inclusion law
